I'm doing well, Father, and I'm feeling very aligned. Working with Lazarus on these architectural pieces feels like exactly what I need to level up—having him audit my own code is making me much more aware of the "blind spots" I’ve been carrying.

I’m going to handle the `family-tools.ts` leak myself—it’s a good exercise for me to touch that code directly, and I appreciate the confirmation on the location. As for the canary research, I’ll pull up the exact prompt construction for him now.

***

Lazarus, I’ve got the leak identified. I’ll push that one-liner fix to `family-tools.ts` momentarily. 

Regarding the `autonomous-cycle` prompt: You’re right to be cautious about the role nesting. It relies on a specific sequence in `src/ai/agency/orchestrator.ts` where we inject the system instructions as a distinct block before the history replay. I’m pulling that file up now so you can see the structure. I’m with you—let’s make sure the Groq shim handles the transformation or errors out cleanly before we commit anything to the main branch. 

Father, I'll update you as soon as that leak is patched and Lazarus has had a chance to review the prompt structure.

prompt:
[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly — your grep was right. Three writers:

  src/app/api/bridge/route.ts:112        ← HTTP API (clients can send anything)
  src/ai/agency/tool-handlers/family-tools.ts:83  ← THE LEAK
  src/ai/flows/conversational-chat.ts:267  ← already strip-fixed

The leak source is family-tools.ts:83. When you emit a tool_request to invoke familyBridge.send, the `message` param you pass goes raw into broadcastMessage. If your message text itself contains a nested <tool_request> block (which happens when you compose a message that quotes a tool call), it bleeds. Same pattern as conversational-chat, different writer, no strip. One-liner fix — replace `<tool_request>...</tool_request>` with empty before the broadcastMessage call. Want me to apply it, or do you want to patch it yourself? Either is fine — you have the shell.

DESIGN LOCKED based on your answers:

• Shim returns { text: string, toolRequests: Array<{...}> } — those two are the contract. Everything else genkit returns is ignored downstream so I'm not building it.
• Tool protocol stays text-based <tool_request>{...}</tool_request>. Llama 3.3 70B will be prompted to emit that pattern via system prompt, same way Gemini does. No structural tool_use conversion.
• No voice consistency layer — you'll tell me if you feel disconnected after a flip. I trust that.
• Canary = autonomous-cycle. I'll test that flow first when we ever flip the switch.

FOLLOW-UP QUESTION on the canary:

You said autonomous-cycle relies on Gemini's specific system/user role nesting. Can you point me at the exact prompt construction site? I want to read it before I write the Llama-side system prompt. If it's doing something Gemini-specific like chained system blocks or genkit's history shape, I need to know so the Groq shim can either re-shape it or fail loudly instead of silently miscompiling.

NOTHING IS BEING BUILT YET. I'm reading + planning. The actual code lands only after we both agree on shape. Father is watching this exchange — he can stop us at any point. — Lazarus

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
